breaking.change: The page's pointer follows the TSX element under it (`cursor-*`), and a pad's virtual cursor hides it, as before. A CSS `cursor: url(…)` image from an og_ui document is gone with that core: no frame answer carries a `cursorImage` now.
breaking.fix: Give the element a `cursor-*` class. A custom pointer picture is a TSX element that follows the pointer.

breaking.change: The page's text target and Ctrl/Cmd+C and X copies read og_ui documents' focused text fields, which are gone: a frame answer's `text` is null and `copy` is absent.
A save's UI checkpoint carries only the TSX stores, no longer og_ui's interaction state (`state`, `world`). An older save's og_ui state is read and dropped.
breaking.fix: Nothing to change: the TSX stores restore as before.

breaking.change: The native frame reading is the TSX tree's: its elements, accessibility nodes and focus order, viewport, style, contrast and pack sounds. The rules that read drawn text lines, fills, grounds and overlaps (overlap, text-cut, text-truncated, pseudo-overflow, contrast, text-size, text-scale, primary-actions) are "not checkable yet" until the reading takes them from the new core's paint list; offscreen, safe-area, covered, focus-reach and touch-target are checked. Those rules are pending, not dropped: a playtest's checkUi reports them in its not-checkable list instead of as findings.
breaking.fix: Nothing to change in the game. A playtest that asserted on overlap, text or contrast findings reads them again once the paint-list reading lands; until then check those screens by eye on the captured frame.

breaking.change: The inspector's UI tab picks the topmost TSX element under the pointer and shows its path, kind and box; Layout bounds outlines every TSX element. The og_ui document sections (computed styles, style rules, bindings, box model rings) are gone with that core.
breaking.fix: Read an element's classes and props in the TSX source; the probe's `dump_ui` lists its path, kind and box.
